disclaimer: Extra SAE-generic scanner copy. Pointers, not a parts list. Not Identifix. Not a cart.

rows.title: Fuel volume regulator control circuit
rows.layperson: The computer cannot drive the fuel-volume regulator. Rail pressure will drift. This is a circuit first, not a tank drop.
rows.doNotThrowParts: Do not drop the tank for a control-circuit code. Power, ground, and the solenoid ohms come first.
rows.firstLook: Command the regulator. Measure voltage at the connector. Then the valve.
rows.sayThis: I have P0001 stored. I want commanded vs actual rail pressure and the regulator circuit test before anyone drops the tank.
rows.askTheShop: Ask for commanded vs actual rail PSI and the ohms at the regulator before a pump module.

rows.title: Fuel volume regulator performance
rows.layperson: The regulator is being driven but rail pressure is not following. A sticky valve or a weak pump — the test decides.
rows.doNotThrowParts: Do not buy a pump and a regulator on the same visit without commanded vs actual.
rows.firstLook: Graph commanded vs actual rail pressure at idle and under load.
rows.sayThis: I have P0002 stored. I want the rail-pressure graph before a pump and a regulator both land on the ticket.
rows.typicalCause: Sticky regulator, weak pump, bad rail sensor
rows.askTheShop: Ask which number failed — commanded vs actual — before two fuel parts.

rows.title: Exhaust cam actuator circuit (Bank 1)
rows.layperson: The computer cannot drive the exhaust VVT solenoid on Bank 1. Oil and that solenoid beat a timing job.
rows.doNotThrowParts: Do not quote a chain because the exhaust actuator circuit failed. Oil screen and the solenoid first.
rows.firstLook: Oil level and quality, then the exhaust solenoid ohms.
rows.sayThis: I have P0013 stored. I want oil condition and the exhaust VVT solenoid test before anyone opens the front cover.
rows.askTheShop: Ask them not to pair intake and exhaust actuators unless both failed a test.

rows.title: Exhaust cam timing over-retarded (Bank 1)
rows.layperson: The exhaust cam is late. Sludged oil or a stuck exhaust actuator is the cheap end. Chain stretch is the expensive one.
rows.doNotThrowParts: Do not authorize a chain until they write the correlation degrees.
rows.firstLook: Oil, exhaust solenoid, then measured cam angle.
rows.sayThis: I have P0015 stored. I want the exhaust cam correlation degrees before a timing-set quote.
rows.typicalCause: Oil, exhaust VVT actuator, chain slack
rows.askTheShop: Ask for commanded vs actual exhaust cam angle in writing.

rows.title: Crank / cam correlation (Bank 2)
rows.layperson: Crank and Bank 2 cam disagree. That can be a $40 sensor or a jumped chain on that bank.
rows.doNotThrowParts: Do not pre-approve a motor. The waveform on Bank 2 decides.
rows.firstLook: Scope Bank 2 cam vs crank. Write the degrees.
rows.sayThis: I have P0018 stored. I want the Bank 2 scope print before anyone quotes a chain or a motor.
rows.typicalCause: CMP sensor, tone ring, timing chain
rows.askTheShop: Ask which sensor waveform failed and whether slack was measured.

rows.title: Crank / cam correlation (exhaust / Bank 2)
rows.layperson: Crank and Bank 2 exhaust cam disagree. Sensor versus mechanical is still the fork.
rows.doNotThrowParts: Do not throw a sensor and a chain in the same visit without a scope print.
rows.firstLook: Scope exhaust cam Bank 2 against crank.
rows.sayThis: I have P0019 stored. I want the exhaust-cam waveform on Bank 2 before a timing quote.
rows.askTheShop: Ask for the scope print, not 'these chains fail a lot.'

rows.title: Camshaft actuator circuit (Bank 2)
rows.layperson: Bank 2's intake VVT solenoid circuit failed. If Bank 1 is clean, that bank's oil-control valve is the cheap end.
rows.doNotThrowParts: Do not replace Bank 1 and Bank 2 hardware because one circuit set a code.
rows.firstLook: Oil, Bank 2 solenoid ohms, then the actuator.
rows.sayThis: I have P0020 stored. I want the Bank 2 VVT solenoid circuit test — not a pair of actuators.
rows.askTheShop: Ask why both banks need hardware when only Bank 2 set the code.

rows.title: Camshaft timing over-retarded (Bank 2)
rows.layperson: Bank 2's cam is late. Oil and that bank's actuator first. Chain is the expensive branch.
rows.doNotThrowParts: Do not swap a chain because Bank 2 is late. Ask for the correlation degrees.
rows.firstLook: Oil, Bank 2 solenoid, measured cam angle.
rows.sayThis: I have P0022 stored. I want Bank 2 cam correlation degrees before a timing-set quote.
rows.askTheShop: Ask for commanded vs actual on Bank 2 only.

rows.title: O2 heater control circuit (B1S2)
rows.layperson: The computer cannot drive the heater in the rear Bank 1 sensor. Monitors may not finish. This is not a converter.
rows.doNotThrowParts: Do not quote a brick for a rear-heater circuit. Heater ohms first.
rows.firstLook: Fuse, heater ohms on B1S2, then the sensor.
rows.sayThis: I have P0036 stored. I want the B1S2 heater ohms before anyone prices a converter.
rows.askTheShop: Ask which sensor position (B1S2) so nobody replaces all four.

rows.title: O2 sensor signals swapped (Bank 1 / Bank 2)
rows.layperson: The computer thinks the upstream sensors are on the wrong banks. Usually a harness swap after a prior repair.
rows.doNotThrowParts: Do not buy two sensors. Confirm which connector is Bank 1 on paper.
rows.firstLook: Trace the harness labels. Command one heater and watch which PID moves.
rows.sayThis: I have P0040 stored. I want the bank labels confirmed on the harness before any sensor order.
rows.askTheShop: Ask them to prove the connectors are on the correct banks — not to replace both sensors.

rows.title: O2 heater control circuit (B2S1)
rows.layperson: Bank 2's upstream heater circuit failed. Fuel control stays sloppy until that sensor warms. Not a converter.
rows.doNotThrowParts: Do not throw a cat from a heater circuit. Ask for heater ohms on B2S1.
rows.firstLook: Fuse, heater ohms, then the sensor.
rows.sayThis: I have P0050 stored. I want the B2S1 heater ohms and the bank written on the RO.
rows.askTheShop: Ask which side of this engine is Bank 2 on paper.

rows.title: MAP / MAF / throttle correlation
rows.layperson: Airflow, manifold pressure, and throttle position do not agree. A dirty MAF, a cracked boot, or a throttle body that is lying.
rows.doNotThrowParts: Do not replace the throttle, the MAF, and the MAP as a set. Graph all three.
rows.firstLook: Idle vs 2500 RPM: MAF g/s, MAP, TPS. Then a smoke test.
rows.sayThis: I have P0068 stored. I want MAF, MAP, and throttle graphed together before anyone prices a throttle body.
rows.typicalCause: Intake leak, dirty MAF, throttle carbon
rows.askTheShop: Ask which of the three signals failed the correlation — not a three-part package.

rows.title: Ambient air temperature sensor circuit
rows.layperson: The outside-air sensor circuit failed. HVAC and some fuel strategies use it. Not an engine-out.
rows.doNotThrowParts: Do not quote a climate control module for an ambient-sensor circuit.
rows.firstLook: Live ambient PID vs a thermometer at the bumper.
rows.sayThis: I have P0070 stored. I want the bumper sensor reading vs a thermometer before a climate module.
rows.typicalCause: Ambient sensor, harness in the bumper
rows.askTheShop: Ask for the live PID next to an actual temperature.

rows.title: Fuel pressure regulator 1 control circuit
rows.layperson: The computer cannot drive the fuel-pressure regulator. Rail pressure will not follow command.
rows.doNotThrowParts: Do not drop a tank for a control-circuit code. Measure at the connector.
rows.firstLook: Power and ground at the regulator. Then commanded vs actual.
rows.sayThis: I have P0090 stored. I want the regulator circuit test before a pump module.
rows.askTheShop: Ask for ohms and voltage at the regulator plug.

rows.title: Fuel system leak — large
rows.layperson: The computer sees a large fuel-side leak. A cracked line or a loose fitting after a filter job is more common than a tank.
rows.doNotThrowParts: Do not replace the tank from a leak code. Find the wet spot.
rows.firstLook: Smell and sight along the rail and the filter fittings. Then a pressure-hold.
rows.sayThis: I have P0093 stored. I want the leak location named before anyone prices a tank.
rows.typicalCause: Loose fitting, cracked line, rail seal
rows.askTheShop: Ask where it is wet. 'Needs a tank' without a location is a stall.

rows.title: MAF sensor high input
rows.layperson: The airflow meter is reporting more air than the engine can be eating, or the signal is shorted high.
rows.doNotThrowParts: Do not throw a MAF and a computer. Unplug and re-measure.
rows.firstLook: Unplug the MAF. If the code changes to low, the sensor or its power is the story.
rows.sayThis: I have P0103 stored. I want the unplugged-vs-plugged reading before a MAF and a PCM both land on the ticket.
rows.typicalCause: MAF short, oil on the wire, harness
rows.askTheShop: Ask for g/s at idle vs spec with the meter live.

rows.title: MAP sensor circuit
rows.layperson: The manifold-pressure signal is missing or out of range. Connector and vacuum hose come before the sensor.
rows.doNotThrowParts: Do not replace the MAP without key-on engine-off vs baro.
rows.firstLook: KOEO MAP vs barometric pressure. Then the hose.
rows.sayThis: I have P0105 stored. I want key-on MAP vs baro before anyone buys the sensor.
rows.askTheShop: Ask for KOEO MAP next to baro. They should match within a few kPa.

rows.title: Intake air temperature circuit
rows.layperson: The IAT circuit failed. Often the same part as the MAF. The engine will run rich or lean until it is honest.
rows.doNotThrowParts: Do not quote a computer for an IAT circuit. Live temp vs a thermometer.
rows.firstLook: Live IAT vs a thermometer at the air box.
rows.sayThis: I have P0110 stored. I want the live intake-air temperature next to a thermometer before a MAF.
rows.askTheShop: Ask whether this car uses a MAF-combo IAT so they do not buy two parts.

rows.title: Engine coolant temperature circuit
rows.layperson: The coolant-temp circuit failed. Fans, gauge, and fuel strategy can all lie. Electrical until proven otherwise.
rows.doNotThrowParts: Do not throw a thermostat from a circuit code. Live temp vs a probe.
rows.firstLook: Live ECT vs an infrared or probe reading on the metal.
rows.sayThis: I have P0115 stored. I want live coolant temp against a probe before a thermostat lands on the invoice.
rows.askTheShop: Ask for the live PID next to a real temperature. A flush is not this repair.

rows.title: Throttle / pedal position sensor A circuit
rows.layperson: Throttle-position sensor A is unhappy. Limp mode is common. Dual-signal throttle bodies fail one side at a time.
rows.doNotThrowParts: Do not quote a computer first. Graph both TPS signals.
rows.firstLook: Dual TPS graph. Then the pedal pair if this is drive-by-wire.
rows.sayThis: I have P0120 stored. I want both throttle-position signals graphed before a new PCM.
rows.askTheShop: Ask for the dual-signal graph. A new computer is not the first move.

rows.title: O2 sensor high voltage (B2S1)
rows.layperson: Bank 2 upstream is pinned rich. A soaked connector or a real rich condition on that bank.
rows.doNotThrowParts: Do not throw four sensors. Ask for Bank 2 fuel trims next to the sensor voltage.
rows.firstLook: Fuel trims both banks. Then force lean and watch B2S1.
rows.sayThis: I have P0152 stored. I want Bank 2 fuel trims next to the sensor voltage before a set of O2 sensors.
rows.askTheShop: Ask for both banks' trims side by side.

rows.title: O2 sensor slow response (B2S1)
rows.layperson: Bank 2's upstream sensor is lazy. Age, or a small exhaust leak on that bank fooling it.
rows.doNotThrowParts: Do not sell a converter from a slow upstream sensor. Leak check that bank first.
rows.firstLook: Graph B2S1. Smoke the manifold on that bank.
rows.sayThis: I have P0153 stored. I want a leak check on Bank 2 before anyone prices a converter.
rows.typicalCause: Lazy O2, exhaust leak before the sensor
rows.askTheShop: Ask them to smoke or listen for a manifold leak before a brick.

rows.title: O2 sensor no activity (B2S1)
rows.layperson: Bank 2 upstream is flat-lined. Sensor or heater. The converter is a separate test.
rows.doNotThrowParts: Do not bundle a converter into a dead upstream sensor.
rows.firstLook: Heater fuse and ohms on B2S1. Then the sensor.
rows.sayThis: I have P0154 stored. I want the B2S1 heater test before a converter is even mentioned.
rows.askTheShop: Ask whether the heater fuse is good. A dead heater makes a healthy sensor look dead.

rows.title: O2 sensor circuit (B2S2)
rows.layperson: Bank 2's rear sensor circuit failed. This sensor watches the converter; it does not convict it.
rows.doNotThrowParts: Do not quote a Bank 2 brick for a rear-sensor circuit.
rows.firstLook: Fix the sensor. Re-run the monitor.
rows.sayThis: I have P0156 stored. I want the rear Bank 2 sensor fixed and the monitor re-run before a converter quote.
rows.askTheShop: Ask them to prove the brick separately.

rows.title: O2 sensor high voltage (B2S2)
rows.layperson: Bank 2's rear sensor is pinned rich or shorted. Sometimes the sensor; sometimes a soaked connector.
rows.doNotThrowParts: A high rear sensor is not a converter invoice. Prove the brick.
rows.firstLook: Unplug and re-measure. Then the catalyst monitor.
rows.sayThis: I have P0158 stored. I want the rear sensor proved before anyone prices a Bank 2 converter.
rows.askTheShop: Ask them to prove the brick separately. A high rear sensor is not a converter.

rows.title: O2 sensor no activity (B2S2)
rows.layperson: Bank 2's rear sensor is flat. Sensor or heater. The converter is a separate test.
rows.doNotThrowParts: Do not bundle a converter into a rear-sensor repair on Bank 2.
rows.firstLook: Heater ohms on B2S2. Then the sensor.
rows.sayThis: I have P0160 stored. I want B2S2 heater ohms — not a second converter on the same ticket.
rows.askTheShop: Ask for the specific sensor position in writing.

rows.title: Fuel rail pressure sensor range / performance
rows.layperson: The rail-pressure sensor does not match what the pump is doing. Sensor versus pump is the fork.
rows.doNotThrowParts: Do not throw a pump from a sensor-performance code. Mechanical gauge vs PID.
rows.firstLook: Tee a mechanical gauge. Compare to the PID.
rows.sayThis: I have P0191 stored. I want a mechanical rail gauge next to the PID before a pump.
rows.askTheShop: Ask for commanded vs actual and a mechanical reading.

rows.title: Injector circuit — general
rows.layperson: An injector circuit failed but the computer did not name the hole. Isolate before buying a set.
rows.doNotThrowParts: Do not buy a set of injectors from P0200. Name the cylinder.
rows.firstLook: Which cylinder incremented the misfire counter. Then that injector's ohms.
rows.sayThis: I have P0200 stored. I want the cylinder named and that injector's ohms before a set.
rows.askTheShop: Ask which hole failed. A six-pack is a sales habit.

rows.title: Engine over-temperature
rows.layperson: The computer saw coolant too hot. A stuck thermostat, low coolant, or a dead fan — not a 'flush package' first.
rows.doNotThrowParts: Do not authorize a water pump and a flush from an overtemp code. Level, fan, thermostat graph.
rows.firstLook: Coolant level cold. Fan command. Temperature graph.
rows.sayThis: I have P0217 stored. I want coolant level, fan command, and a temperature graph before a pump-and-flush ticket.
rows.askTheShop: Ask for the temperature graph and whether the fan actually spun.

rows.title: Throttle position sensor B range / performance
rows.layperson: The second throttle-position signal does not match sensor A. Drive-by-wire limp is common.
rows.doNotThrowParts: Do not quote a PCM because one of two throttle signals drifted. Graph A vs B.
rows.firstLook: TPS A vs TPS B through a pedal sweep.
rows.sayThis: I have P0221 stored. I want throttle sensors A and B graphed together before a computer.
rows.askTheShop: Ask for the dual-signal print. A pedal sensor is a different part.

rows.title: Fuel pump secondary circuit low
rows.layperson: The fuel-pump power circuit is low. Relay, fuse, or a pump that is pulling the voltage down.
rows.doNotThrowParts: Do not drop the tank until voltage at the pump connector is written down.
rows.firstLook: Voltage at the pump with it commanded on. Then the relay.
rows.sayThis: I have P0231 stored. I want voltage at the pump connector before anyone drops the tank.
rows.typicalCause: Relay, fuse, pump draw, inertia switch
rows.askTheShop: Ask for voltage at the pump, not just 'needs a pump.'

rows.title: Turbo boost sensor A range / performance
rows.layperson: The boost-pressure sensor does not match commanded boost. A hose off the sensor beats a new turbo.
rows.doNotThrowParts: Do not quote a turbo from a sensor-performance code. Hose and sensor first.
rows.firstLook: Key-on boost vs baro. Then the reference hose.
rows.sayThis: I have P0236 stored. I want key-on boost vs baro and the sensor hose checked before a turbo.
rows.askTheShop: Ask for commanded vs actual boost and whether the hose is on.

rows.title: Knock sensor 1 circuit low
rows.layperson: Knock sensor 1 is quiet or shorted low. The computer may pull timing. It is not automatically a spun bearing.
rows.doNotThrowParts: Do not quote an engine from a knock-sensor circuit. Circuit test first.
rows.firstLook: Sensor ohms and the harness at the block.
rows.sayThis: I have P0327 stored. I want a knock-sensor circuit test before an engine estimate.
rows.askTheShop: Ask for a circuit test before an engine estimate.

rows.title: Knock sensor 2 circuit
rows.layperson: The other knock sensor circuit failed. Same rule: electrical first, not a bottom-end.
rows.doNotThrowParts: Do not replace both sensors and a computer from one circuit.
rows.firstLook: Which bank is sensor 2 on this engine. Then ohms.
rows.sayThis: I have P0330 stored. I want knock sensor 2 identified on paper and ohm'd before a pair.
rows.askTheShop: Ask which bank sensor 2 serves on this VIN.

rows.title: Camshaft position sensor low input
rows.layperson: The cam sensor signal is low or missing. Connector and oil-soaked pins beat a timing job.
rows.doNotThrowParts: Do not quote a chain from a low cam signal. Scope first.
rows.firstLook: Connector, then the waveform, then the tone ring.
rows.sayThis: I have P0342 stored. I want the cam-sensor waveform before a timing job.
rows.typicalCause: CMP sensor, oil in the connector
rows.askTheShop: Ask them to scope the signal before quoting a timing job.

rows.title: Exhaust camshaft position sensor (Bank 1)
rows.layperson: The exhaust cam sensor on Bank 1 is unhappy. Sensor versus a damaged tone ring.
rows.doNotThrowParts: Do not throw intake and exhaust sensors as a pair unless both failed.
rows.firstLook: Exhaust CMP waveform. Then the tone ring.
rows.sayThis: I have P0365 stored. I want the exhaust cam waveform on Bank 1 — not a pair of sensors.
rows.askTheShop: Ask which cam (intake vs exhaust) and which bank.

rows.title: Secondary air injection system
rows.layperson: The cold-start air pump is not moving air. Common on cars that live with snow and salt. Not a converter.
rows.doNotThrowParts: Do not quote a converter. This is a cold-start emissions pump.
rows.firstLook: Command the pump. Listen. Check the valves.
rows.sayThis: I have P0410 stored. I want the air pump commanded and the check valves tested — not a converter.
rows.typicalCause: Air pump, check valves, seized fittings
rows.askTheShop: Ask them to command the pump. A brick is the wrong aisle.

rows.title: Fuel level sensor circuit
rows.layperson: The tank sender circuit failed. The gauge lies and some emissions monitors will not run.
rows.doNotThrowParts: Do not drop a tank for a circuit code until the live PID is written down.
rows.firstLook: Live fuel-level PID vs an actual fill.
rows.sayThis: I have P0460 stored. I want the live fuel-level PID vs an actual fill before a tank drop.
rows.askTheShop: Ask whether the sender is sold separately from the pump on this VIN.

rows.title: EVAP flow during non-purge
rows.layperson: Vapor is flowing when the purge valve should be shut. A stuck-open purge valve is the usual ending.
rows.doNotThrowParts: Do not replace the canister for a purge-flow-when-closed code. Command the valve shut.
rows.firstLook: Command purge closed. Watch fuel trims. Then the valve.
rows.sayThis: I have P0496 stored. I want the purge valve commanded closed before a canister quote.
rows.askTheShop: Ask them not to replace the canister for a purge valve that will not seat.

rows.title: Brake switch A / B correlation
rows.layperson: The two brake-switch signals disagree. Cruise and torque management get confused. A $20 switch is common.
rows.doNotThrowParts: Do not quote an ABS module from a brake-switch correlation.
rows.firstLook: Both switch PIDs while pressing the pedal.
rows.sayThis: I have P0504 stored. I want both brake-switch PIDs before an ABS module.
rows.askTheShop: Ask for switch A vs B while the pedal moves.

rows.title: Oil pressure sensor low
rows.layperson: The oil-pressure sensor reads low. A $30 sender or a real pressure problem. A mechanical gauge decides.
rows.doNotThrowParts: Do not quote a bottom-end from a sender code. Mechanical gauge first.
rows.firstLook: Mechanical oil-pressure gauge hot idle vs spec.
rows.sayThis: I have P0522 stored. I want a mechanical oil-pressure number before an engine estimate.
rows.typicalCause: Sender, low oil, real pressure loss
rows.askTheShop: Ask for PSI on a mechanical gauge, not the dash light.

rows.title: System voltage high
rows.layperson: Charging voltage is too high. A regulator or an aftermarket alternator. Modules get cooked if you ignore it.
rows.doNotThrowParts: Do not replace three modules from high voltage. Fix the charge voltage first.
rows.firstLook: Voltage at the battery at idle and 2000 RPM.
rows.sayThis: I have P0563 stored. I want charging voltage at the battery before anyone prices modules.
rows.askTheShop: Ask for volts at idle and 2000 RPM. Over ~15.5 V is the story.

rows.title: Control module performance
rows.layperson: The engine computer failed an internal check. Voltage events create a lot of these. A reflash or a real PCM — voltage first.
rows.doNotThrowParts: Do not quote a PCM before charging-system numbers and a TSB check.
rows.firstLook: Battery/alternator numbers. Then TSB / reflash.
rows.sayThis: I have P0607 stored. I want charging-system numbers and a TSB check before a PCM.
rows.askTheShop: Ask for system voltage and a TSB check for a reflash before a module.

rows.title: Fuel pump A control circuit / open
rows.layperson: The computer cannot drive the fuel-pump control circuit. Relay and the control wire beat a tank drop.
rows.doNotThrowParts: Do not drop the tank for an open control circuit. Voltage at the pump first.
rows.firstLook: Relay, inertia switch, voltage at the pump connector.
rows.sayThis: I have P0627 stored. I want voltage at the pump connector before a tank drop.
rows.askTheShop: Ask for voltage at the pump with the pump commanded.

rows.title: Sensor reference voltage A circuit
rows.layperson: The 5-volt reference that feeds several sensors is unhappy. One shorted sensor can take the whole reference down.
rows.doNotThrowParts: Do not replace the PCM first. Unplug sensors on that 5V rail until the reference returns.
rows.firstLook: Measure the 5V rail. Unplug suspects one at a time.
rows.sayThis: I have P0641 stored. I want the 5-volt rail isolated sensor-by-sensor before a PCM.
rows.askTheShop: Ask which sensor pulled the 5V down. A new computer is last.

rows.title: Malfunction indicator lamp circuit
rows.layperson: The check-engine bulb or its driver circuit failed. The light may be dark while codes are stored.
rows.doNotThrowParts: Do not quote a PCM for a bulb circuit. Prove the lamp.
rows.firstLook: Command the MIL on. Check the bulb or cluster pixel.
rows.sayThis: I have P0650 stored. I want the MIL commanded on before a cluster or a PCM.
rows.askTheShop: Ask them to command the lamp. A dark bulb is not a computer.

rows.title: ECM / PCM power relay control circuit
rows.layperson: The engine computer's power relay circuit failed. No-start or a computer that goes to sleep. Relay first.
rows.doNotThrowParts: Do not quote a PCM before the power-relay pins are measured.
rows.firstLook: Relay click, fuse, voltage at PCM power pins.
rows.sayThis: I have P0685 stored. I want voltage at the PCM power pins before a computer.
rows.askTheShop: Ask for voltage at the PCM power pins and whether other modules are also silent.

rows.title: Transmission range sensor performance
rows.layperson: The gear-selector sensor does not match the shifter. The trans may limp or refuse to start in Park.
rows.doNotThrowParts: Do not rebuild a transmission from a range-sensor code. Cable and sensor first.
rows.firstLook: Shifter cable adjustment. Then the range-sensor PIDs.
rows.sayThis: I have P0706 stored. I want the shifter cable and range-sensor PIDs before a transmission rebuild.
rows.askTheShop: Ask for P/R/N/D PIDs while they move the lever.

rows.title: Transmission fluid temperature sensor performance
rows.layperson: The trans-fluid temperature reading is implausible. A $40 sensor or a real overheat — they are different bills.
rows.doNotThrowParts: Do not flush a transmission from a TFT-performance code. Live temp vs a case reading.
rows.firstLook: Live TFT vs an infrared on the pan after a drive.
rows.sayThis: I have P0711 stored. I want live trans-fluid temp vs a case reading before a flush.
rows.askTheShop: Ask for the live PID next to a real temperature. A flush is not automatic.

rows.title: Input / turbine speed sensor no signal
rows.layperson: The computer cannot hear the input-shaft speed sensor. Shift quality dies. Sensor versus a failed trans.
rows.doNotThrowParts: Do not rebuild from a no-signal code. Scope the sensor first.
rows.firstLook: Sensor ohms and the waveform in gear.
rows.sayThis: I have P0717 stored. I want the input-speed waveform before a rebuild.
rows.askTheShop: Ask for the waveform in Drive. A silent sensor is not a rebuild.

rows.title: Output speed sensor no signal
rows.layperson: The output-shaft speed sensor is silent. Speedo and shift scheduling suffer. Sensor first.
rows.doNotThrowParts: Do not rebuild from a silent output sensor. Waveform first.
rows.firstLook: OSS waveform while rolling. Then the tone ring.
rows.sayThis: I have P0722 stored. I want the output-speed waveform while rolling before a transmission quote.
rows.askTheShop: Ask for the rolling waveform, not a rebuild package.

rows.title: Gear 2 incorrect ratio
rows.layperson: Second gear is slipping or the ratio is wrong. Clutch pack, solenoid, or a speed-sensor lie.
rows.doNotThrowParts: Do not approve a rebuild until they name which clutch failed a test.
rows.firstLook: Input vs output speed in 2nd. Fluid condition. Then the solenoid.
rows.sayThis: I have P0732 stored. I want input vs output speed in second and which clutch failed before a rebuild.
rows.askTheShop: Ask which clutch or solenoid failed. 'Needs a rebuild' is not a test.

rows.title: Torque converter clutch solenoid circuit
rows.layperson: The lock-up solenoid circuit failed. Shudder or a flare at cruise. Circuit first, not a converter by default.
rows.doNotThrowParts: Do not throw a torque converter from a solenoid-circuit code. Ohms first.
rows.firstLook: TCC solenoid ohms and command.
rows.sayThis: I have P0743 stored. I want the lock-up solenoid ohms before a converter.
rows.askTheShop: Ask for solenoid ohms. A converter is a different test.

rows.title: High-voltage interlock circuit
rows.layperson: The high-voltage interlock opened. A service plug, a connector, or a crash switch. High-voltage work only.
rows.doNotThrowParts: Do not probe orange cables. Do not clear and deliver. This is a safety interlock.
rows.firstLook: Shop with HV training. Service-plug and interlock continuity.
rows.sayThis: I have P0A0D stored. I want a high-voltage-trained shop to check the interlock — I will not authorize a driveway probe.
rows.typicalCause: Service plug, HV connector, interlock switch
rows.askTheShop: Ask for a shop with high-voltage training. A 12V scan is not the whole job.

rows.title: Hybrid battery pack over-temperature
rows.layperson: The hybrid pack ran too hot. Cooling fan, intake filter, or a real pack problem. Filter first on a lot of these.
rows.doNotThrowParts: Do not quote a pack from one overtemp. Cooling path first.
rows.firstLook: Pack intake filter and fan command. Then module temps.
rows.sayThis: I have P0A7E stored. I want the pack cooling filter and fan commanded before a battery-pack quote.
rows.askTheShop: Ask for module temperatures and whether the cooling fan actually ran.

rows.title: Hybrid / EV isolation fault
rows.layperson: High-voltage isolation to chassis failed. Moisture, a damaged cable, or a pack issue. Safety item. HV shop only.
rows.doNotThrowParts: Do not authorize a 12V parts cannon. Isolation is high-voltage diagnosis.
rows.firstLook: HV-trained shop. Isolation megger. Then the wet connector.
rows.sayThis: I have P0AA6 stored. I want a high-voltage isolation test from a trained shop — not a 12V parts list.
rows.askTheShop: Ask for isolation megohms and which circuit leaked. A can of cleaner is not a guess.

rows.title: Left rear wheel-speed sensor
rows.layperson: The left-rear wheel-speed sensor is unhappy. ABS and traction will drop out on that corner.
rows.doNotThrowParts: Do not throw an ABS module from one corner. That sensor and the ring first.
rows.firstLook: LR sensor ohms and the tone ring through the window.
rows.sayThis: I have C0036 stored. I want the left-rear wheel-speed sensor and tone ring checked — not an ABS module.
rows.typicalCause: LR sensor, tone ring, harness at the knuckle
rows.askTheShop: Ask for that corner's sensor ohms and a look at the ring.

rows.title: ABS pump motor circuit
rows.layperson: The ABS pump motor circuit failed. The pump may be seized or the relay is dead. Not four sensors.
rows.doNotThrowParts: Do not throw four wheel-speed sensors from a pump-motor code.
rows.firstLook: Pump command, relay, current draw.
rows.sayThis: I have C0115 stored. I want the ABS pump commanded and the current draw written before a module.
rows.askTheShop: Ask whether the pump spins and what it draws. Four sensors are the wrong aisle.

rows.title: Yaw-rate sensor
rows.layperson: The yaw-rate sensor that stability control uses is unhappy. Calibration after a windshield or a module swap is common.
rows.doNotThrowParts: Do not quote an ABS module before a yaw calibration is attempted.
rows.firstLook: Calibration procedure. Then the sensor.
rows.sayThis: I have C0196 stored. I want a yaw-rate calibration before an ABS module.
rows.askTheShop: Ask if this car needs a calibration after glass or a battery.

rows.title: Driver airbag deployment loop
rows.layperson: The driver-airbag circuit failed a continuity check. The SRS light stays on. Safety item.
rows.doNotThrowParts: Do not probe airbag circuits. Do not clear and deliver. Clock spring vs bag is the fork.
rows.firstLook: SRS-trained shop. Clock-spring resistance per the book.
rows.sayThis: I have B0010 stored. I want an SRS-trained shop to measure the clock spring — I will not authorize a clear-and-deliver.
rows.typicalCause: Clock spring, driver airbag, connector under the wheel
rows.askTheShop: Ask them not to probe the yellow connectors with a parts-store meter.

rows.title: Passenger airbag deployment loop
rows.layperson: The passenger-airbag circuit failed. Occupancy sensor and the bag loop are different tests.
rows.doNotThrowParts: Do not replace the bag and the occupancy mat as a pair without naming which loop failed.
rows.firstLook: Which loop (bag vs occupancy). SRS shop.
rows.sayThis: I have B0013 stored. I want the passenger-bag loop named separately from the occupancy mat.
rows.askTheShop: Ask which loop failed. A mat is not a bag.

rows.title: Left side-impact sensor
rows.layperson: The left side-impact sensor circuit failed. The side bags may be disabled. Safety item.
rows.doNotThrowParts: Do not clear an SRS light to see if it comes back. The light is the safety part.
rows.firstLook: SRS shop. Sensor ohms and the rocker harness.
rows.sayThis: I have B0090 stored. I want the left impact-sensor circuit tested — do not clear and hand back the keys.
rows.askTheShop: Ask why the module is unhappy before anyone clears the code.

rows.title: Lost communication with vehicle dynamics / VSC
rows.layperson: The stability-control module is silent. ABS and traction will drop out. Power and the bus first.
rows.doNotThrowParts: Do not replace the module before the fuse and the power pins.
rows.firstLook: Fuse/power at the stability module. Then lone vs clustered U-codes.
rows.sayThis: I have U0122 stored. I want power at the stability module before a replacement.
rows.askTheShop: Ask whether U-codes are clustered (bus-wide) or lone.

rows.title: Lost communication with power-steering control
rows.layperson: The electric power-steering module is silent. Assist may die. Voltage and the module connector first.
rows.doNotThrowParts: Do not quote a steering rack before voltage at the EPS connector.
rows.firstLook: Battery state-of-charge. EPS power pins. Then the module.
rows.sayThis: I have U0131 stored. I want voltage at the power-steering module before a rack.
rows.askTheShop: Ask for charging-system numbers. Quiet EPS is often a dying battery.
